title: Analysis of the immune status in the whole blood of cancer patients
summary:
The human body's immune system protects against disease by recognizing and fighting pathogens such as viruses and bacteria.   It can also recognize and destroy defective cells in the human body. These can be cancer cells, for example. If this is not successful, cancer can develop. The cells of the immune system are called white blood cells. 
In this study, we want to investigate the significance of the activity of white blood cells in the blood for the progression of cancer. Blood samples will be taken from cancer patients before and after cancer treatment. After the blood is taken, it is exposed to different stimuli that trigger certain reactions in the white blood cells. We want to find out whether the strength of these reactions is influenced by the cancer and whether conclusions can be drawn about the course of the disease and the success of the treatment. This knowledge could help to tailor cancer treatment to individual patients.
conditions: Tumors of the liver, bile ducts, intestines, pancreas

interventions.name: In patients with tumors of the liver, bile ducts, intestine or pancreas, 1.2 ml of blood is collected before and after chemotherapy or surgery. The blood is treated in vitro with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) or phytohaemagglutinin (PHA). The resulting production of interleukin-6 (IL-6) or interferon-gam
Blood will be collected once from healthy subjects and assayed as in Arm 1. The values obtained will be used as a reference.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients requiring surgical or chemotherapeutic treatment for cancer of the liver, bile ducts, intestines or pancreas.
Exclusion criteria:
Minors, pregnant women, persons incapable of giving consent
